text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered: canary-deploy-2028-03 - 502 spike detected in canary pool (eu-west-1). Threshold: 5% -> current: 18%. PD incident created: INC-7821

pagerduty: New page fired for INC-7821 - urgent

sara: got the page - looking at canary metrics now. seeing 502s around 12:32 UTC.

tom: @sara what was the last deploy tag for the canary? I see rollout started ~12:15.

sara: tag is release/2028.03.14-canary. healthchecks started failing after ~12:28.

mike: paging in - i'm on call rotation takeover. will coordinate. assign me as responder on PD.

pagerduty: INC-7821 acknowledged by mike

jess: quick check: logs show ``upstream returned error 502`` from model-proxy. stacktrace snippets: ``grpc error: upstream reset`` repeated.

eng-oncall: running quick smoke tests against production canary, a subset of requests are hitting model runtime OOMs (OOMKill). linking pod logs.

qa: reproduction on staging with same image shows increased memory use over baseline after ~30s of runtime. probable memory leak / regressive change in tokenizer cache.

mike: decision time - revert canary or scale? Can we roll back just the canary image?

sara: we can rollback canary to release/2028.03.08 which was stable. I can start rollback if we want immediate mitigation.

tom: recommend rollback + keep canary disabled until we root cause. also create a temporary rate limit to reduce traffic to canary if rollback takes >5m.

mike: agree. sara, please run: ``kubectl -n inference rollout undo deploy/canary-svc --to-revision=20280308`` and monitor pods.

sara: running rollback now. command output: ``deployment "canary-svc" rolled back
rolling restart triggered``

incident-bot: Deploy rollback initiated by sara. Notifying PD and posting to thread.

eng-oncall: pods are terminating and new pods coming up. initial pods show HEALTH checks passing on /healthz. 2/3 new pods ready.

jess: observing error rate dropping from 18% -> 6% in the last 4 minutes. still elevated but trending down.

mike: good. I'll keep PD assigned until rates are back to baseline (<2%). can we route remaining canary traffic to stable while we confirm?

sara: temporarily set routing policy to 0% canary traffic. updating router config: ``/configs/routing set canary_weight=0``. applying... done.

incident-bot: Routing updated: canary_weight=0 (applied by sara).

qa: running end-to-end checks across eu-west-1. login flows and generation tests passing.

jess: error rate now 1.5% overall for the service in eu-west-1. looks stable.

tom: notify support/customer-success to prep comms? any customers affected?

mike: initial PD notes say 6 accounts hit elevated latency/5xx for ~10 mins. low volume customers flagged. I'll draft a short blurb.

sara: leaving the canary image rolled back and disabled. creating ticket to revert the new image to a branch for deeper debug: TKT-5412.

pagerduty: INC-7821 resolved by mike (ack->resolve).

mike: marking incident SEV3. postmortem owner: jess. Please add timeline, root cause hypothesis (tokenizer cache regression causing memory growth), and remediation steps (fix leak, add CI mem regression test, canary resource limits).

jess: got it — will open postmortem doc and schedule follow-up with infra/rls team for tomorrow.

eng-oncall: handoff to tom in 10m for follow-up monitoring.

tom: taking over monitoring. will escalate to eng-sre if anything reoccurs. :thumbsup:

mike: thanks all. closing the live thread — add any follow-ups to TKT-5412 and the postmortem.

incident-bot: Thread closed (no active responders).
